newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Rising prices, higher U.S. ratings fuels forestry.
newsitem.headline: Rising prices, higher U.S. ratings fuels forestry.

text.p: Rising fine paper prices and a higher trading recommendation on some North American forestry companies was behind a rally in Sweden's forestry sector on Tuesday, analysts said.
On Tuesday morning Sweden's forestry index rose 2.40 percent compared to a general index move of 0.93 percent.
"Mead (a U.S. forestry company) raised prices for uncoated (fine) paper by $50 a tonne," Nordbanken forestry analyst Erik Magnusson told Reuters.
"Furthermore the forestry index in the U.S. has not been as good as the Dow Jones index lately...also the higher recommendation from investment bank Morgan Stanley played a part."
Another analyst said he had thought for a long time that forestry company prices were cheap and now Morgan Stanley appeared to agree.
"Morgan Stanley, which for a long time has been negative on forestry shares, has upgraded a lot of companies in the U.S.," he said.
On Monday Morgan Stanley said it was upgrading trading recommendations on Champion International, Mead Corp and Consolidated Papers from 'neutral' to 'outperform'.
On the Stockholm bourse on Tuesday, MoDo shares climbed six to 234 crowns, Stora gained three to 102.50, SCA rose 4.5 to 170 crowns.
